correctness.rationale: For any n−1-wise fair signs, Fourier–Walsh inversion leaves only the full-product character theta; its order-n moment contribution is exactly theta*n!*product(coefficients). The independent-sign 2k moment is strictly improved when any unequal squared-coefficient pair is averaged, because conditional pair expansion (2) has nonnegative coefficients and its h=k>=2 term is strictly increasing in q_i*q_j; thus equal squared magnitudes uniquely maximize it. AM–GM controls and characterizes the theta product correction, with compatible sign alignment. This proves the exact bound and all equality cases. An exact-rational finite verifier passed 210 instances; it is not used as a proof of the unbounded family.

originality.rationale: The novel scope is a uniform, exact conditional sharp moment constant at the final level of proper independence for every even length at least six, including the full interaction continuum and every coefficient extremizer. The n=4 endpoint and proper-moment matching are older special cases and are not presented as standalone novelties. Full-text comparison with Pass–Spektor 2014/2017 and Spektor 2016 found pairwise/three-wise bounds or zero-sum conditioning, not the exact n−1-wise parity-parametric endpoint. Relevant published record summaries address four-way persistence, low-independence tails or Walsh flatness, none implying the general stated theorem. Historical hidden equivalence is a disclosed residual risk.

value.rationale: For every even length at least six, this gives the sharp exact endpoint Khintchine functional inequality for the natural last proper-independence level, a nontrivial family omitted by sharp k<=3 cases. The formula completely parametrizes the remaining interaction, classifies all optimal coefficient magnitudes and signs, and yields exact L^n/L^2 constants for even-cycle Walsh edge spaces, the first even moment detecting their cycle relation. It is structurally more than moment matching, a routine special case or a few computed constants; the covered n=4 endpoint is not the standalone claim.
